document.title: fix(jslib): handle timers that clear themselves from their callback
document.summary: `run_timeouts` now holds its own reference to the callback during the call and re-looks-up the timer id afterwards, and `set_timeout_impl` no longer hands a just-cleared id back out.
document.why: A timer callback that clears its own id makes `run_timeouts` re-add an interval with a freed `JSValue` or double free a one-shot ([#40](source:s1)).

sources.title: Timer callback that clears itself causes double free / freed JSValue reuse
sources.gist: After the call, re-look-up the id and only reschedule or free when the entry still exists; extend the timer harness.

sources.label: PR #61
sources.gist: Dup func during the call, re-look-up after, stop reusing cleared ids; five new harness scenarios.

groups.title: run_timeouts survives callbacks that mutate the timer map
groups.why: The issue asks `run_timeouts` to reschedule or free only entries that still exist after the callback ([#40](source:s1)).
groups.summary: `run_timeouts` calls a dup of the entry's `func`, then re-looks-up the id and reschedules in place or frees, and the harness drives self-clearing, sibling-clearing, and timer-creating callbacks through it.
lookFor: Subtle: the `JS_DupValue` around `JS_Call` is not in the issue; QuickJS `JS_Call` takes no reference, so a callback that clears itself would otherwise free its own running closure.
Intervals are now rescheduled by writing `next_scheduled_at` through a pointer taken after the call, not by `hmput` of a pre-call copy, so no pointer into `timeout_hm` lives across the callback.
On `main` the new harness aborts with `gc_decref_child: Assertion 'p->ref_count > 0' failed` on the self-clearing scenarios.

groups.title: Cleared ids are not reused immediately
groups.why: The post-call re-lookup in `run_timeouts` is only sound if a replacement timer created in the callback cannot take the id that just ran.
groups.summary: `set_timeout_impl` post-increments `timeout_id_counter`, so the next timer gets a fresh id even when the previous one was cleared.
lookFor: Behavior change no source mentions: `setTimeout` returning 1, `clearTimeout(1)`, then `setTimeout` now returns 2 instead of 1; the `self-clearing timeout scheduling a replacement` scenario fails without it.

commits.subject: fix(jslib): handle timers that clear themselves from their callback
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
run_timeouts kept a copy of the TimeoutItem across the JS call, then rescheduled or freed it. A callback that cleared its own id had already freed func, so intervals were re-added with a freed JSValue and one-shots were double freed. Hold a reference for the duration of the call, re-look-up the id afterwards, and only reschedule or free an entry that still exists. Stop reusing an id right after it is cleared, so a replacement timer created in the callback is not mistaken for the one that just ran.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
